topic: Question 5.11 on non-symmetric Strong Spectral Property for even looped double paths
title: Koljančić–Oblak Question 5.11 (arXiv:2604.21552v1, Section 5): nSSP witnesses for looped double paths

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: Question 5.11 of Koljančić and Oblak (arXiv:2604.21552v1, Section 5; journal p. 776) has an affirmative answer: every even double path with a nonempty loop set allows the non-symmetric Strong Spectral Property. We construct a symmetric one-loop witness using coprime branch continuants and prove injectivity of its characteristic-polynomial differential. Openness then supplies every prescribed nonempty loop set. The same argument gives a complete existence criterion in odd order: at least one loop must lie at an odd-numbered vertex. The witnesses can be chosen symmetric with positive integer nonzero entries. Carptopus (19 August 2026) previously proved the full existence criterion and its single-loop spectral characterization. We give an explicit integer construction, an arithmetic criterion for unit edge weights, and the three-way classification for the central-loop and interior-loop families.
summary: The allowing criterion is nonempty loops in even order and an odd-numbered loop in odd order, with symmetric positive-integer witnesses. The earlier proof is credited to Carptopus (19 August 2026). Unit edge weights with one loop at ell give nSSP exactly when gcd(ell,n+1)=1. Central-loop and interior-loop families receive full three-way classifications.
